splash.upgrading: Upgrading your data. With a large library this can take a few minutes; please keep LectureFlow open…
error.start.title: LectureFlow could not start
error.start.body: The background service did not start. You can try again; if it keeps happening, the logs show the reason.
error.crash.title: The background service stopped unexpectedly
error.crash.body: Unfinished tasks are kept and continue from where they stopped after a restart.
error.page.title: The page could not be loaded
error.page.body: The background service is still running. You can load the page again.
error.data_dir.title: The data folder cannot be reached
error.data_dir.body: LectureFlow keeps its data in {path}, which cannot be reached now. If it is on an external drive, connect the drive and try again.
error.location.title: The data folder setting cannot be read
error.location.body: The contents of {path} are not recognised. So as not to show an empty library, LectureFlow did not switch to the default location. Correct or delete this file, then try again; without it the default location {default} is used.
reason.timeout: The background service did not respond within 30 seconds.
reason.not_found: The background service program was not found: {path}
reason.spawn_failed: The background service program could not be run ({code}): {path}
reason.exit_code: The background service exited with code {code}.
reason.port: Several ports in a row could not be used.
reason.token_rejected: The background service rejected the access token.
reason.bad_mode: The background service is not running in desktop mode.
reason.restart_loop: The background service kept asking to be restarted.
reason.unwritable: The data folder could not be created: {path}
startfail.data_dir_in_use: Another LectureFlow (process {pid}) is using this data folder: {path}. Close it first (another window, web mode, or a background process that has not exited yet), then click Try again.
startfail.data_dir_in_use_nopid: Another LectureFlow is using this data folder: {path}. Close it first (another window, web mode, or a background process that has not exited yet), then click Try again.
startfail.data_dir_newer: This data folder comes from a newer version of LectureFlow (database version {found}; this version supports up to {known}). So as not to damage your data, LectureFlow did not open it. Install the newer version. To keep using this version, quit LectureFlow and move lectureflow.db out of the data folder to somewhere safe, together with lectureflow.db-wal and lectureflow.db-shm next to it (if there are any). Then copy the backup made before the upgrade, in {path}, into the data folder and rename it to lectureflow.db (only that one file).
startfail.upgrade_backup_no_space: Before upgrading your data, LectureFlow backs up the database, but there is not enough disk space: about {need} GB is needed and the disk of {path} has {free} GB free. Nothing was upgraded or changed. Free up some space, then click Try again.
startfail.upgrade_backup_failed: Before upgrading your data, LectureFlow backs up the database to {path}, but the backup failed, so nothing was upgraded or changed. The details below give the reason; once it is fixed, click Try again.
startfail.db_busy: The database file {path} is in use by another program, and LectureFlow could not use it even after waiting a few seconds. It may be another LectureFlow (an older version or web mode included), a database viewer, or backup, sync or antivirus software working on the file. Nothing was changed. Close those programs (or wait until they finish), then click Try again.
startfail.db_readonly: The database file {path} cannot be written: the file or the data folder is set to read-only, or this account is not allowed to change it. Another program (backup, sync or antivirus software) may also be holding it open. Clear “Read-only” in the file’s properties and make sure this account can change the files in the data folder, then click Try again. If another program is using it, wait a moment and click Try again.
startfail.db_not_a_database: {path} is not a usable database file: it is damaged or has been replaced by another file. LectureFlow left it as it is. If {backups} holds a backup (lectureflow-before-….db, saved automatically before an upgrade or a data import), quit LectureFlow and move this file somewhere safe, together with lectureflow.db-wal and lectureflow.db-shm next to it (if there are any); then copy the backup into the data folder and rename it to lectureflow.db (only that one file). Without a backup, move those files away together and start again: LectureFlow then starts with an empty library. Always move them together: a leftover lectureflow.db-wal would be written into the new database and damage it.
startfail.db_cant_open: The database file {path} cannot be opened. Another program (backup, sync or antivirus software) may be holding it open, this account may not have access to the data folder, or the drive it is on (an external or network drive) is not connected. If another program is using it, wait a moment and click Try again; otherwise check the data folder’s permissions and the drive, then click Try again.
startfail.db_disk_full: The disk of the database file {path} is full, so the database cannot be written. Free up some space, then click Try again.
startfail.db_io_error: The disk failed while reading or writing the database file {path}. Make sure the drive is connected and working (check external and network drives in particular), then click Try again. If it keeps happening, the disk may be failing: back up the data folder soon.
close.detail: If they continue in the background, you will be notified when they finish. Quitting stops them; they continue from where they stopped the next time you open LectureFlow.
close.detail_downloads: If they continue in the background, fetching goes on. Quitting stops it. The sign-in data for the recording site is kept in memory only, so each recording that has not been fully fetched has to be resumed from its own recording page: open the page again and click the LectureFlow extension.
close.detail_both: If they continue in the background, you will be notified when a lecture has been processed. Quitting stops them. The sign-in data for the recording site is kept in memory only, so each recording that has not been fully fetched has to be resumed from its own recording page: open the page again and click the LectureFlow extension. The other tasks continue from where they stopped the next time you open LectureFlow.
close.remember: Remember my choice (you can change it in Settings)
background.title: LectureFlow is working in the background
background.body.win32: Open it again from the icon in the notification area.
background.body.darwin: Open it again from the Dock.
restore.detail: LectureFlow will use the default location {path}. location.json is renamed to {backup} (with a date added if that name is taken); no data is deleted, and renaming the file back restores the old setting.
startup.unsupported_args.title: LectureFlow cannot start with this command line
startup.unsupported_args.body: LectureFlow was started with {switches}, which it does not support, so it closes. Remove the above from the command line (for example in the shortcut) and start LectureFlow again.
startup.sandbox_disabled.title: LectureFlow cannot start with the sandbox turned off
startup.sandbox_disabled.body: The environment variable ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX is set. Any value counts, including 0 or false. LectureFlow runs only with the sandbox on, so it closes. Remove the variable in the system's environment variable settings, or in the script or terminal that starts LectureFlow. Then close and reopen the terminal or program you start LectureFlow from, and start LectureFlow again.
